invariants: Every project-scoped work, asset, screen, reference, benchmark, component, and system record must resolve to exactly one Project relation before it can be treated as project canon.
Project pages expose only Project-filtered linked views; unfiltered master views belong under the system-master area.

Project Registry is an AI/System identity master and must not be used as the default human Project Home; the human landing surface is physically separate from Registry rows that carry machine or automation metadata.

Human Project Home must not expose Codex/local paths, ports, raw SHAs, Record Keys, revisions, prompts, AI notes, hashes, implementation paths, raw CI receipts, or equivalent AI/System metadata as default human-facing content.

Normal project navigation is shallow by default: Project Hub to Human Project Home to project-specific Domain Workspace to Detail or Record; normal L4+ page nesting is avoided and requires explicit exception review.

A Human Project Home remains self-contained and directly exposes the full game or story flow, core systems and necessary setting, and project-specific core data tables; drilldown links cannot replace core understanding.
Domain Workspaces use project-specific names, normally number four through six, and must contain responsibility/context rather than acting as empty folder pages.
Parallel work across different projects uses Project namespace isolation and must never write through another Project relation.
Core-system records use a deterministic Record Key scoped by Project and record type; duplicate keys fail closed instead of being guessed or merged.
Same-record AI writes compare Revision and Last Edited immediately before a bounded record-level update; a stale read aborts instead of overwriting newer human or agent changes.
A successful Notion write requires destination readback of Project, Record Key, Revision, and intended changed fields before completion may be reported.

Notion is the primary human-facing canon for project overview, visual direction, visual asset catalogs, budget tables, tier tables, core-system human models, human-editable flow maps, and storyboards.
Repository Markdown, JSON, game data, code, scenes, resources, tests, and runtime evidence remain the structured and implementation canon for their domains.
The Visual Map may be derived from structured records, but the approved Notion view is the primary human-facing representation for visual planning and review.

When an actual image, mockup, diagram, or visualization exists and is approved for project use, completion requires upload or attachment to the project Visual Bible or project-scoped Asset record, Approved-state recording, and destination readback; a text-only art-direction approval does not fabricate an image requirement.

A Notion edit that requires structured data, Markdown, code, scene, resource, test, or runtime behavior to change must be synchronized into a Codex implementation handoff before implementation or runtime claims.
Image or file delivery success requires write completion plus readback before success may be reported.
Repository code, runtime data, scenes, resources, tracked implementation assets, builds, and tests remain runtime truth.

The default Notion workflow stays within ZERO_INCREMENTAL_COST and must not require paid-only Notion features; Project-filtered views plus search/fetch and destination readback are the baseline fallback.

GPT owns planning, research synthesis, adversarial review, implementation specification, image generation or editing, approved-visual delivery, and final implementation review; GPT does not own product code or runtime implementation.

When implementation or coding exists, Codex is the implementation executor and must rehydrate current GitHub and relevant Notion canon before persistent mutation; a user handoff request is not required to activate this normal implementation phase.
Codex must not generate or generatively edit project images. It may consume only visuals approved for the current use and actually attached or uploaded in Notion with destination readback.

If a required visual is missing, Codex returns a GPT_VISUAL_REQUEST and may continue independent implementation, but must not synthesize an unapproved substitute; GPT creates or edits the visual and Notion approval plus upload/readback precedes Codex consumption.

The retired GPT to PowerShell to local Codex bootstrap path must not be reintroduced as the default project workflow; implementation shell, CLI, MCP, engine, and test execution belong to the Codex execution environment.
When visuals materially affect PoC/demo judgment, representative UX/UI states and approved visual inputs are reviewed in Notion before implementation and runtime validation remains separate.
Project Home is self-contained for core human understanding; child pages are drilldown/evidence, not a substitute for the Home explanation.

Project-management local/HTML surfaces, Figma, and Google Sheets are retired or migration-only; QA Evidence Studio code may remain historical or specialist reference, but active/default project validation routes through REPOSITORY_NATIVE_EVIDENCE_CAPTURE instead of the Studio.
